headline: Local opposition has led to the cancellation of at least 260 billion dollars of planned US data centre projects this year, by the count of the news site Heatmap.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 4: the figure was first reported on 6 Oct 2026 and ran in our 7 Oct 2026 edition at score 8, and the 16 Oct Quartz repeat shows no new facts.
importance_line: It suggests that residents' opposition now decides whether many data centre projects get built, which matters to local governments, developers and investors, but the number comes from one outlet's own survey and has no independent confirmation.
summary: Heatmap News first reported on 6 Oct 2026, from its Heatmap Pro survey of public records, that at least 260 billion dollars of US data centre investment was cancelled this year after sustained local opposition, about half of it in the three months to 30 Sep, and that roughly 1 trillion dollars more faces serious opposition; our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried it, and Quartz repeated the figure on 16 Oct 2026. Heatmap says its figures are probably an undercount because only about 60 percent of projects disclose their size, and the industry group Data Center Coalition did not respond before publication.
notes: Quartz (the pool source, 16 Oct 2026) returned 403; the original Heatmap report was read in full instead and is credited as the first reporter. Older news: first reported 6 Oct 2026 and run in our 7 Oct 2026 edition; no new fact seen in the Quartz headline. Score lowered because it is a repeat.
